title: POC scoping: multilingual legal document extractor - Zenith Fabric
summary: AE+SE (Redwood) and Zenith Fabric scoping a POC to extract structured clauses and obligations from multilingual legal contracts. Discussed required precision/recall targets, daily volume and concurrency, shortlisted open models, tradeoffs around quantization and latency vs cost, and security requirements (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run a benchmark harness over 2 weeks and share pricing/security pack.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sam Riley (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Ana Silva (Zenith Head of ML), Marco Delgado (Zenith Infra), Sofia Chen (Zenith Legal Ops)

Summary / auto notes (auto-generated, may be rough):
- POC: extract clauses, obligations, and party metadata from contracts in English/Spanish/Portuguese.
- Success criteria: entity F1 > 0.8 on clause extraction for core clause types; exact-match > 0.7 for obligations; latency p95 < 1.2s per query in hosted scenario; batch throughput targets for nightly bulk processing.
- Workload: 10k documents/day peak, average doc 1,200 tokens, peak concurrency 120 requests/min.
- Model shortlist: Llama 3 13B fine-tuned, Mistral-Instruct variants, Falcon-180B-lite (quant), small ensemble for Spanish/Portuguese fallback.
- Security: prefer VPC private deployment for production; Redwood Dedicated considered; require SAML SSO, KMS integration, SOC2 artifacts.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Sam Riley: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about an hour, i'll kick off, i'm sam riley from redwood, account exec.
[00:08] Ana Silva: hi, ana here, thanks for making time. quick context, we are a legal-tech platform for fabric manufacturers, we ingest supplier contracts and need a robust extractor for clauses and obligations across english spanish portuguese.
[00:22] Priya Kapoor: great, thanks ana. quick intro — i'm priya kapoor, solutions engineer, i'll drive the benchmark side and the model selection.
[00:29] Marco Delgado: marco — infra. i'll be answering questions about our network and whether we can host on prem.
[00:34] Sofia Chen: sofia from legal ops — i'll focus on the compliance and discovery requirements.

[00:40] Sam Riley: agenda for today — success criteria, volume and sizing, shortlist models and tradeoffs, security/deployment, and next steps. sound good?
[00:47] Ana Silva: sounds good.

[01:02] Priya Kapoor: to start with success criteria, what's the business metric? is it reducing manual review time, exact clause recovery, downstream automation accuracy?
[01:12] Ana Silva: mostly reducing manual triage — we need high precision on obligations so compliance team doesn't miss something. target is reduce manual triage by 60%, and for the POC we want demonstrable extraction quality: entity/phrase F1 >= 0.8 for the 12 clause types we care about, and obligation exact-match >= 0.7.
[01:35] Sam Riley: good to hear explicit numbers. are you planning to use the extractor in a synchronous API flow (end-user web) or as offline bulk processing?
[01:45] Ana Silva: both. day-to-day the UI queries will be interactive, but we also have nightly batch processing for historical ingests. interactive latency ideally under 1.2 seconds p95, nightly throughput should handle 10k docs per day.
[02:03] Marco Delgado: to add, peak concurrency for the UI could hit 120 concurrent calls during morning processing windows.

[02:20] Priya Kapoor: perfect — we usually size POC runtimes differently for interactive vs batch. A couple of clarifying q's: what's average tokens per doc? and do the docs include scanned images (OCR)?
[02:30] Ana Silva: avg 1,200 tokens. about 15% are scanned PDFs, we run internal OCR to plaintext before ingest — for the POC we'll provide OCR outputs.

[02:45] Sam Riley: on model choices, priya, i'll let you walk through the shortlist and tradeoffs.
[02:49] Priya Kapoor: sure. our recommended shortlist for this workload — focusing on open models — is: 1) Llama 3 13B fine-tuned with instruction layer for extraction tasks; 2) Mistral-Instruct 7B or 12B with a small fine-tune; 3) a quantized Falcon derivative for high throughput (we call it falcon-lite in notes); and 4) a cascade option where we run a smaller multilingual model for quick tagging and escalate to the larger model for ambiguous cases.
[03:20] Ana Silva: are there models that handle spanish/portuguese better out of the box?
[03:25] Priya Kapoor: Mistral variants tend to generalize well multilingual, Llama 3s have good instruction-following but may need extra spanish/pt fine-tuning. for the POC we suggest a 2-model approach: baseline on Llama 3 13B tuned on your bilingual dataset, and a fallback Mistral-12B for Portuguese edge cases.
[03:45] Marco Delgado: curious about quantization — how much quality do we lose at 4-bit? we care a lot about exact obligations.
[03:53] Priya Kapoor: short answer, some drop in entity-level precision with aggressive 4-bit quant, especially for rare proper nouns and legalese; 8-bit or structured quant (QLoRA-style) preserves more quality. we can run a small A/B to measure exact-match drop; usually for obligation extraction we recommend 8-bit or mixed precision for production.
[04:15] Sam Riley: also tradeoff is cost — 8-bit means more RAM/gpu but better quality; 4-bit is cheaper for dedicated pools.
[04:22] Ana Silva: what's your hosted latency for a Llama 3 13B at p95?
[04:28] Priya Kapoor: on hosted with our optimized runtime and batching disabled for interactive calls, p95 is around 700-900ms for 1,200-token docs on a 13B kernal we use, but that can creep up with concurrency. With dedicated reserved capacity we can guarantee lower variance.
[04:45] Marco Delgado: if we go private on-prem, what changes?
[04:48] Priya Kapoor: on-prem you manage hardware — our private package includes the control plane and the inference runtime that can run in a VPC or air gap. latency will depend on your GPUs; we provide the same batching and kernel tuning. security-wise on-prem satisfies stricter residency and SOC2-like policies but adds operational responsibility.
[05:06] Sofia Chen: for compliance — we need SAML SSO, audit logs, and key management integration. do you support external KMS/HSM?
[05:14] Sam Riley: yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support KMS integrations and we have an HSM pattern in our enterprise guide. we'll share the security pack.
[05:21] Sofia Chen: also need e-discovery readiness — retain audit trail for two years.
[05:25] Priya Kapoor: we can surface per-request audit logs in the console; retention is configurable via enterprise add-on.
[05:31] Ana Silva: ok, back to benchmarks — priya, what will you run and how long will it take?
[05:36] Priya Kapoor: plan: we run a two-week benchmark. week 1: offline quality runs over your 200 labeled samples to measure entity F1 and obligation exact-match across candidate models and quant settings. week 2: performance runs simulating interactive concurrency and nightly batch throughput — p50/p95/p99 latency + cost per doc.
[05:53] Sam Riley: we also propose sampling real documents for edge-case discovery, and run a small user study with legal ops to validate downstream triage reduction.
[06:01] Ana Silva: timeline — we want POC results in 6 weeks. is that feasible?
[06:05] Priya Kapoor: feasible: we usually take 2 weeks to prep datasets and run week 1 quality benchmarks, 1 week to refine prompts/fine-tune small checkpoints, 2 weeks for perf runs and integration, and 1 week for analysis and reporting — total ~6 weeks.
[06:22] Marco Delgado: cost estimate ballpark? we need to budget for dedicated or private.
[06:26] Sam Riley: ballpark for a 6-week POC with dedicated reserved test pool and 13B model variants is in the low tens of thousands USD — we'll send a formal quote. for hosted runs it can be less but with less isolation.
[06:40] Ana Silva: i want a clear pass/fail criteria: we will call POC successful if entity F1 >= 0.8 on labeled set and production-like p95 latency <= 1.2s in hosted sim.
[06:51] Priya Kapoor: noted — we'll include that as gating metrics in the benchmark report.
[06:56] Sofia Chen: one more on data handling — can you guarantee data not persisted for hosted runs? some hosted vendors keep corp data for model training.
[07:03] Sam Riley: good question — our hosted API can be configured to opt-out of training/retention for enterprise customers; dedicated/private gives full data isolation. we'll include the legal language in the security pack.
[07:15] Marco Delgado: networking — if we do dedicated, will we need a peering link for low latency?
[07:20] Priya Kapoor: for dedicated we offer several networking modes: public with IP allowlists, VPC peering, and private interconnect depending on region. we'll validate with infra.
[07:31] Ana Silva: any concerns about hallucinations in legal text? false obligations are a big risk.
[07:36] Priya Kapoor: yes, hallucination risk is real; our eval focuses on precision for obligation extraction and we include adversarial prompt sets to surface hallucination tendencies. also we recommend a verification step — a small rule-based post-processor to reduce false positives and an uncertainty score for human triage.
[07:55] Sam Riley: ok let's capture decisions: 1) two-model approach for POC (Llama 3 13B tuned + Mistral-12B fallback); 2) prefer 8-bit quant for initial runs; 3) run 2-week benchmark with metrics above; 4) security pack and sample data to be exchanged.
[08:14] Ana Silva: agreed.
[08:18] Priya Kapoor: any blockers for data sharing? do you have NDAs or data masking needs?
[08:22] Ana Silva: NDA signed, will share masked documents for the initial run, but we can provide full redacted sets under SRA for later stages.
[08:33] Marco Delgado: i'll look into whether on-prem is needed; for the POC we prefer dedicated hosted to start.
[08:40] Sofia Chen: and legal will review the data processing addendum once you send it.
[08:45] Sam Riley: perfect. we'll send the security pack, SSO guide, and a link to the benchmark repo. brief note on the benchmark harness — it measures entity F1, exact-match for obligations, and also outputs per-case confidence scores that we can threshold.
[08:58] Priya Kapoor: also we'll include prompt templates and example evaluation labels. for fine-tuning we recommend small adapter-style fine-tunes to keep model size manageable.
[09:10] Ana Silva: do you support model ensembling or cascades in the runtime?
[09:14] Priya Kapoor: yes, our routing supports cascades and model variants — we can route quick calls to the small model and escalate to large when confidence low. cost-aware routing policies are supported.
[09:24] Ana Silva: perfect. any red flags?
[09:27] Sam Riley: only operational items — we need your sample contracts, infra constraints, and legal check on DPA. once we have those we'll kick off.
[09:36] Marco Delgado: i can share infra notes by monday.
[09:39] Sam Riley: bam. okay let's wrap with explicit next steps — (recap) sam send security pack by 4/25, priya share harness by 4/27, ana upload samples by 4/28, schedule kickoff 4/29.
[09:55] Ana Silva: noted, thanks.
[09:58] Sofia Chen: thanks everyone.
[10:02] Sam Riley: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and the quote.

Auto-questions (may be partial):
- Q: what is POC success threshold? A: entity F1 >= 0.8; obligations exact-match >= 0.7; p95 latency <= 1.2s in hosted sim.
- Q: timeline? A: 6 weeks to POC deliverable.

References mentioned in call: security pack, SOC2 artifacts, benchmark harness repo (link to be shared), sample contracts (Zenith shared drive).

End of transcript.
